sections.title: Current conclusion
sections.markdown:
Reviewed 31 October 2026: a partially framed original 1822 will has now been inspected; it names son John and Wilson’s widow, without resolving Mary’s birth surname or parents. See the dated source review below.

James Glasgow's 1775 will directly names his wife **Mary**. The 1817-1818 Wilson
inheritance pleadings say Mary was a daughter of one of Archibald Wilson's six
sisters. Because James's mother Rachel was another sister, the pleaded
relationships make James and Mary first cousins.

Neither the will nor the equity papers gives Mary the birth surname
Crozier/Crosier or identifies her mother. Preserve Mary as James's wife and as a
daughter of an unidentified Wilson sister, but treat the `Crosier-512` surname
and exact parentage as unproved.

sections.title: Original 1822 will: readable family clauses — 31 October 2026
sections.markdown:
The readable continuation of Mary Glasgow’s will names her son John Glasgow to manage her property and gives a remainder to Mary Glasgow, described as the widow of deceased Wilson Glasgow, and her heirs. The will is dated 5 April 1822; the recorded probate is 14 October 1822. Mary’s existing Newberry family and the probate four days after her reported gravestone death make Mary, wife of James (Crosier-512), the compatible maintained account. The named son is compatible with John Glasgow-1146; the widow is compatible with Mary McCracken-3711, widow of Wilson Glasgow-1982. These identifications are family-context inferences, not additional relationship clauses.

The opening on manuscript page 489 runs below the framing of the inspected scan; the following page begins mid-clause. This is a partial reading, not a complete transcription or complete heir list. A Robert Glasgow witnesses the will and proves it; that role is not a statement that he is a son, and no exact Robert profile is assigned. The readable text neither supplies Mary’s birth surname nor identifies her parents. It does not name Tennessee Robert Glasgow-2769 as Archibald’s son or exclude an omitted heir. No father confidence, attachment, mother, vital field or duplicate decision changes.

Sources: [opening, page 489](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:939L-J8SN-1Y) · [continuation and probate, page 490](https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:939L-J8SF-5R). Newberry Will Book H, FamilySearch images 248–249, inspected 31 October 2026.

[John, compatible existing son account](/people/glasgow-1146.html) · [Mary, compatible widow account](/people/mccracken-3711.html) · [Wilson, the existing deceased-husband account](/people/glasgow-1982.html). Their existing relationship assessments are not revised by this record review.

potential_parentage.method: Automated leads use birth surnames—not married surnames—as parental eligibility, role-specific biological age limits, bounded and approximate-date uncertainty, household chronology, specific time-aware localities, mapped distance, tenancy succession, migration destinations and sex-aware Scottish naming positions across generations. People already attached as the subject's parents stay in the identity summary and are excluded from this alternative-candidate list, regardless of relationship confidence. The main calibration uses clues available on disconnected profiles; existing parent and sibling links are retained as comparison context rather than treated as transferable evidence. Common ordered names and grandparent-to-child echoes receive a small non-zero weight, so a John or James match can support several independent criteria without producing a lead alone. Rare names, repeated bearers and bundles across otherwise distinct branches receive substantially more weight according to catalogue frequency. An exact migration place is weighted by its rarity and repetition across both branches; a shared destination country is worth only one point. Extra weight is added only when at least three independent clue types converge: naming, locality, specific migration, household chronology or collateral networks. Sparse profiles retain a clearly labelled chronology-only fallback instead of disappearing. Countries, states, counties and research clusters do not count as a shared locality, and fallback, broad representative or kin-inferred coordinates are excluded from distance scoring. Shared descendant profiles are removed before branch-name comparison. A candidate already recorded as a parent-in-law is excluded. A confident or independently supported parent is treated as settled; uncertain and unassessed attachments remain open to alternative comparison. A different linked parent, an uncle/aunt or grandparent path, and a matching existing child profile prevent an alternative from being classified as a strong direct-parent lead until the underlying tree conflict or duplicate is resolved. Familiar forms such as Bessie are normalised. Surname remains an eligibility filter worth zero points.
potential_parentage.warning: Naming customs, shared farms and occupations are circumstantial. Children, spouses and collateral relatives may be missing, and tree-derived family networks are not independent evidence. Scores rank research leads; they do not prove parentage.
